**Skill this week:** treating mobility as a health exposure. By the end of the week you should be able to tell migrant stock from migrant flow, explain migration with push and pull forces, distance decay and the gravity model, and read a flow map.

## Read

- Chapter 3, Migration
- Dobra A, Bärnighausen T, Vandormael A, Tanser F. Space-time migration patterns and risk of HIV acquisition in rural South Africa. *AIDS.* 2017;31(1):137-145. [doi:10.1097/QAD.0000000000001292](https://doi.org/10.1097/QAD.0000000000001292)

## Map

Complete ArcGIS Online Exercises 3.1 Spatial distributions, 3.2 Push and pull forces, and 3.3 Refugees. The links are at [esri.com/Human-Geography](https://www.esri.com/Human-Geography).

For more practice: Exercise 3.4 Does immigration increase unemployment?

## Public health case

Using the geolocated residential history of every person in the ACDIS cohort, Dobra and colleagues found that HIV risk rose by half at migration distances of 40 km for men and 109 km for women.
